title: Does the layer at which you extract activations for jailbreak detection matter for robustness?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: principled layer selection improves detector robustness and reduces reliance on easily-obfuscated layers. Also reveals at which stage harmful intent becomes linearly separable, informing alignment theory. Each link from 'layer selection' to 'improved safety monitoring' is explicit.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Training multiple linear probes (one per layer) is a repetitive but structured task. Evaluating on standard + paraphrased + GCG prompts uses established benchmarks. Every-4th-layer sampling reduces the work. A beginner with mentor guidance can manage this systematic evaluation.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: layer x attack-type AUROC heatmap. Well-bounded experimental design. The output is a single visualization with clear interpretation. Though multiple probes are needed, each is quick to train.

novelty.reasoning: This question has been substantially addressed. 'Do Internal Layers of LLMs Reveal Patterns for Jailbreak Detection?' (arXiv:2510.06594) directly investigates layer-wise behavior for jailbreak detection. Alert (arXiv:2601.03600) identifies safety-relevant layers and selects discriminative modules, finding middle-to-late layers (12-26) are best. JBShield (USENIX Security 2025) computes embeddings at identified critical layers. The general finding — layer selection matters and middle-to-late layers are optimal — is well-established. The proposed heatmap of layer x attack-type AUROC is a specific visualization but the underlying findings are largely known.
